content.value_statement: OT teams need clear technical scope without unsupported authority or pricing conclusions. This skill builds validated DOCX descriptions and a separate cost-analysis handoff.
actual_capabilities: Builds milestone-based project descriptions for Research, Prototype, and follow-on production Other Transactions.
Converts white papers, SOOs, SOWs, and draft descriptions into OT-focused technical scope.
Creates phased milestones with deliverables, completion evidence, sequence, and pending payment types.
Separates project-description content from pricing, funding, contribution calculations, and cost-analysis routing.
Validates DOCX structure, required sections, tables, placeholders, authority citations, and artifact separation.
Produces a separate chat-only milestone handoff for downstream OT cost analysis.
limitations: Does not choose statutory authority or make Agreements Officer determinations.
Does not create cost estimates, funding profiles, prices, IGCEs, or agreement terms.
Requires a DOCX authoring path, Python with python-docx, and a renderer for complete validation.
Does not guarantee Microsoft Word behavior when validation uses only LibreOffice.

use_cases.title: Structure a New Prototype OT
use_cases.description: Turn an approved prototype concept into phases, milestones, deliverables, and objective completion evidence.

use_cases.title: Convert a Technical White Paper
use_cases.description: Preserve approved technical facts while removing FAR artifact language, staffing details, and pricing content.

use_cases.title: Reduce an Existing Scope
use_cases.description: Compare scope reductions, show technical and schedule effects, and rebuild approved milestones without estimating savings.

prompt_templates.title: Start from a Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an OT project description from this concept: [concept]. Ask for missing authority and scope facts before proposing milestones.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for an early project concept

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Source Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the attached [document type] into an OT project description. Preserve settled technical decisions and exclude all pricing, funding, and FAR artifact content.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for an existing white paper or scope

prompt_templates.title: Design Measurable Milestones
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the confirmed [authority] and project outcome, propose phases and milestones with deliverables, objective completion evidence, dependencies, and pending decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed milestone planning before document generation

prompt_templates.title: Revise and Validate Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise the approved project description using these changes: [changes]. Preserve unaffected decisions, show impacts, obtain milestone approval, then generate and validate the DOCX.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced controlled revision and artifact validation

output_examples.input: Create a Prototype OT description for a software pilot with approved authority but no useful TRL model.
output_examples.output: A decision summary uses observable maturity evidence, lists pending agreement facts, and proposes measurable software milestones before requesting approval.

output_examples.input: Convert a priced SOW into an OT project description without carrying cost data into the agreement artifact.
output_examples.output: The resulting document preserves technical outcomes and acceptance evidence while excluding CLINs, rates, funding, staffing counts, and dollar amounts.

output_examples.input: Reduce an approved prototype scope while keeping the technical baseline and milestone identifiers.
output_examples.output: The revision presents reduction choices with capability, evidence, schedule, and risk effects, then updates only the user-approved milestone structure.

best_practices: Confirm statutory authority and participant facts before deriving scope.
Approve the complete milestone structure before generating the DOCX.
Run structural validation and visual page inspection after every document correction.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to choose authority or make participant-status determinations.
Do not place costs, funding, labor rates, or the chat handoff inside the project description.
Do not claim complete validation when rendering or page inspection was unavailable.

faq.question: Which Other Transaction authorities does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Research OTs under 10 U.S.C. 4021, Prototype OTs under 4022, and follow-on production under 4022(f).

faq.question: Can the skill select the correct authority?
faq.answer: No. The user or Agreements Officer must supply and confirm the authority.

faq.question: Does the project description include cost estimates?
faq.answer: No. It excludes prices, funding, labor rates, contribution calculations, and cost-analysis conclusions.

faq.question: Is TRL required for every project?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses TRL only when supplied or useful, and otherwise relies on observable maturity evidence.

faq.question: What files does the skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces one validated project-description DOCX. The milestone handoff remains in chat and is not saved as a file.

faq.question: How does the skill validate the final document?
faq.answer: It runs the bundled structural validator, renders the DOCX, inspects every page, corrects defects, and repeats available checks.
